scope: Central Texas corridor (McLennan, Bell, Coryell, Brazos counties; Waco, Killeen, Temple, Bryan-College Station) - health & opportunity

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Resident of McLennan, Bosque, Falls, Freestone, Hill, or Limestone County

documents_needed: Proof of extraordinary expenses (medical bills, childcare) if any
records.hours: Crisis line 24 hours a day; walk-in open access at Clifton Street Clinic Mon-Thu 8:00 a.m.-3:00 p.m.
records.cost: Sliding scale based on ability to pay; no one turned away for inability to pay
records.notes: 24-hour crisis line: 1-866-752-3451 (also 988). Walk-in intake is at 1200 Clifton Street, Waco, TX 76704. Fee policy at https://hotbhn.org/about/charges-for-services/.
records.name: Heart of Texas Behavioral Health Network (Local Mental Health Authority)
records.organization: Heart of Texas Behavioral Health Network
records.description_en: The public mental health center for McLennan County. It offers adult and child mental health care, substance use treatment, disability services, and a 24-hour crisis line.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Adults, children ages 3-17, and families in McLennan, Bosque, Falls, Freestone, Hill, and Limestone counties. Fees are based on ability to pay, and no one is turned away for not being able to pay.
records.how_to_apply: Call (254) 752-3451 or toll-free (866) 752-3451 for screening, or walk in to the Clifton Street Clinic (1200 Clifton Street, Waco) Monday-Thursday 8:00 a.m.-3:00 p.m. After hours, press Option 4 when calling.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Resident of Bell, Coryell, Hamilton, Lampasas, or Milam County

documents_needed: Proof of income (paystubs, support letters, disability awards)
Recent hospital discharge paperwork if any
records.hours: Walk-in intake Mon-Fri 8:00 a.m.-3:00 p.m.; crisis hotline 24/7
records.notes: 24/7 crisis hotline: (800) 888-4036. Main line (254) 298-7000 is NOT the crisis line. Killeen intake site: 100 East Ave. A, Killeen, TX 76541. Eligibility from https://centralcountiesservices.org/our-services/adult-mental-health/. Some CCS web pages contain unrelated injected spam text; verify details by phone.
records.name: Central Counties Services (Local Mental Health Authority)
records.description_en: The public mental health center for Bell and Coryell counties. It offers adult and child mental health care, disability services, early childhood intervention, and a 24-hour crisis hotline.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Adults 18+ who live in Bell, Coryell, Hamilton, Lampasas, or Milam County and are uninsured or underinsured. Children ages 3-17 in those counties with serious emotional or behavioral problems.
records.how_to_apply: Walk in for screening and intake Monday-Friday 8:00 a.m.-3:00 p.m. at 304 S. 22nd St, Temple, or 100 East Ave. A, Killeen. Be ready to wait.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Resident of Brazos, Burleson, Grimes, Leon, Madison, Robertson, or Washington County

records.notes: Mailing address P.O. Box 4588, Bryan, TX 77805. Toll free 1-800-282-6467. 24/7 crisis hotline (888) 522-8262.
records.name: MHMR Authority of Brazos Valley (Local Mental Health Authority)
records.description_en: The public mental health and developmental disability center for Brazos County and nearby counties. It runs a 24/7 mental health and substance use crisis hotline and a crisis triage center.
records.eligibility_summary_en: People living in Brazos, Burleson, Grimes, Leon, Madison, Robertson, and Washington counties who need mental health, substance use, or developmental disability services.
records.how_to_apply: For routine mental health services call (979) 361-9815. In a crisis call the 24/7 hotline at (888) 522-8262.

records.notes: Shelters in Killeen (65 beds) and Temple (15 beds); addresses kept confidential. Outreach offices in Killeen, Temple, Gatesville, Hamilton. Site also lists (254) 773-7765. National DV hotline 1-888-799-SAFE.
records.name: Families In Crisis
records.description_en: Emergency shelter, crisis counseling, and housing help for survivors of family violence, sexual assault, and homelessness. It also runs a homeless shelter and rental help in Killeen and Temple.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Survivors of family violence or sexual assault and people without housing in Bell, Coryell, and Hamilton counties. You do not need money, papers, or a police report.
records.how_to_apply: Call or text the 24-hour hotline at (254) 634-1184, or walk in to the Killeen office at 1305 East Rancier Avenue, Mon-Fri 8am-5pm (no appointment needed).

records.notes: Shelter location is not published. Site says it serves Waco and surrounding counties without listing them.
records.name: Family Abuse Center
records.description_en: Emergency shelter and support for people hurt by domestic violence and their children. Services include counseling, case management, support groups, legal help, housing help, and transportation.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Adults and children affected by domestic violence in Waco and surrounding counties.
records.how_to_apply: Call the 24-hour hotline at 1-800-283-8401.

records.notes: General shelter info: (979) 822-1492. Hours not listed on site.
records.name: Twin City Mission
records.description_en: Emergency homeless shelter (The Shelter for Hope), hot meals, rapid re-housing, and domestic violence shelter (Phoebe's Home) in Bryan.
records.eligibility_summary_en: People who are homeless or at risk, and survivors of domestic violence, in the Bryan-College Station area.
records.how_to_apply: For shelter and Coordinated Entry housing assessment, call (979) 822-5482. For domestic violence emergency shelter, call Phoebe's Home at (979) 775-2255.

records.notes: Program hours vary; call ahead.
records.name: Mission Waco
records.description_en: Faith-based nonprofit in Waco offering social services (Meyer Center), supportive housing, clothing vouchers, and youth programs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Low-income and homeless people in Waco.
records.how_to_apply: Call (254) 753-4900 or visit the main office to ask about services.

records.cost: Call to ask; financial services team helps with coverage
records.notes: Clinics in Waco (Bellmead, Central, Elm Ave, Imperial Dr, MacArthur, MLK Jr, S. 18th, West Waco, Women's Health) plus Hillsboro, McGregor, and Temple Downtown. Sliding-fee details were not stated on the pages read.
records.name: Waco Family Medicine
records.description_en: Community health clinics across Waco for primary care, children's care, women's health, dental, behavioral health, lab, and pharmacy. Staff help patients apply for Medicaid, CHIP, and other programs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to the community, including people with Medicaid, CHIP, or no insurance. Ask about payment options.
records.how_to_apply: Call the new patient line at (254) 313-4610 to make an appointment. Same-day and after-hours visits are available.

records.hours: Mon-Thu 8:00 AM-4:00 PM; closed Friday and weekends; by appointment only
records.notes: Email clinic@templecommunityclinic.org.
records.name: Temple Community Clinic
records.description_en: Medical care, health education, and social work services for people without insurance or with limited insurance in Temple.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Uninsured and underinsured Bell County residents.
records.how_to_apply: Call (254) 771-3374 or visit during clinic hours to set up an appointment. New patient forms are on the website.

records.hours: Belton & Killeen: Mon-Thu 7:00 a.m.-4:30 p.m., Fri 7:00 a.m.-11:00 a.m.
records.notes: Killeen Clinic: 309 N. 2nd Street, Killeen, TX 76541. Temple Clinic (820 N. 31st) listed as TEMPORARILY CLOSED. Headquarters: 4236 Lowes Drive, Temple, TX 76502.
records.name: Bell County Public Health District Clinics
records.description_en: Public health clinics offering immunizations, STD testing, pregnancy testing, family planning, and TB services.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Bell County residents. Some services have fees (for example TB testing is $35).
records.how_to_apply: Call (254) 532-9800 or walk in during clinic walk-in times.

records.notes: Phone and address were not listed on the page read; the application PDF has details. Department works with Greater Killeen Free Clinic and Temple Community Clinic.
records.name: Bell County Indigent Health Care Program (CIHCP)
records.organization: Bell County Indigent Health Services Department
records.description_en: County program that helps pay for basic health care for very low-income Bell County residents who do not qualify for other state or federal health programs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Very low-income Bell County residents who do not qualify for Medicaid or other programs.
records.how_to_apply: Download the BCIHCP Application for Assistance from the Bell County Indigent Health Services web page and follow its instructions.

records.hours: Office hours vary; call before visiting. Closed for lunch 12-1 p.m.
records.notes: Mailing: P.O. Box 188, Gatesville, TX 76528.
records.name: Coryell County Indigent Health Care Program
records.description_en: County program that provides health care to qualified low-income residents of Coryell County.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Qualified low-income residents of Coryell County.
records.how_to_apply: Call (254) 865-2883 before visiting to ask about applying.

records.name: McLennan County Indigent Health Care Program (CIHCP)
records.description_en: County program that helps pay for basic health care for low-income McLennan County residents who do not qualify for other programs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Low-income McLennan County residents who meet program rules.
records.how_to_apply: Call (254) 757-5174 or visit the Health Services office to apply.

records.notes: Other clinics: 111 Santa Fe Plaza Drive, Killeen, TX 76541; 36000 Shoemaker Lane Suite 2135, Fort Cavazos, TX 76544. The Copperas Cove WIC clinic closed permanently in August 2025.
records.name: Bell County WIC
records.description_en: Healthy food benefits, nutrition counseling, and breastfeeding help for pregnant women, new moms, babies, and children under 5.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Pregnant women, new mothers, infants, and children under 5 in working or non-working families who meet income, residency, and health screening rules.
records.how_to_apply: Start an application online at texaswic.org/apply; a local WIC team member will call to set your first appointment.

records.hours: Mon, Wed-Fri 8:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m.; Tue 9:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m.; 2nd Saturday 8:30 a.m.-12:30 p.m.
records.notes: Text line: (254) 265-7817. Health District main line (254) 750-5450 also offers immunizations, STI/HIV, and TB clinics.
records.name: Waco-McLennan County Public Health District WIC
records.description_en: Nutrition counseling, food benefits for grocery stores, breastfeeding support, and nutrition classes for moms and young children.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Pregnant women, breastfeeding women with a baby under 1, women who had a baby in the past 6 months, and parents or guardians of children under 5 who meet income rules. Having a job or private insurance does not disqualify you.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online at texaswic.org/apply or call the clinic at (254) 750-5474.

records.notes: Other Brazos County clinics: 29th Street WIC, 4001 E. 29th Street Unit #112, Bryan (979) 255-9872; College Station, 1103 Anderson Street Ste. #102 (979) 255-3804.
records.name: Brazos Valley WIC Clinics
records.description_en: WIC nutrition program clinics in Bryan and College Station with food benefits and nutrition help for moms and young children.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Pregnant women, new moms, infants, and children who are at nutritional risk with income at or below 185% of the federal poverty level.
records.how_to_apply: Call your local clinic to schedule an appointment.

records.notes: New Waco facility (opened Aug 25, 2026) has an on-site market. Food navigation line is multilingual (source: https://www.centraltexasfoodbank.org/get-help). Main office line (512) 282-2111.
records.name: Central Texas Food Bank (Waco & northern counties)
records.description_en: Regional food bank that supplies pantries and mobile pantries, offers SNAP application help, and runs free job training in culinary arts and warehouse work.
records.eligibility_summary_en: People who need food in the food bank's 21-county area, including McLennan, Bell, and Coryell counties.
records.how_to_apply: Use the Find Food Now tool on the website to search by ZIP code, or call 2-1-1 or (877) 541-7905. For SNAP help call (855) 366-3401.

records.notes: Warns of a scam offering discounted Feeding America food boxes on social media.
records.name: Brazos Valley Food Bank
records.description_en: Regional food bank that supplies food pantries, mobile pantries, and school-based pantries in the Brazos Valley.
records.eligibility_summary_en: People who need food in the Brazos Valley area.
records.how_to_apply: Use the pantry map or English/Spanish pantry list on the Find Food page, or call 2-1-1.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: McLennan, Bosque, Freestone, Limestone, Hill, Falls, Ellis, or Navarro County

documents_needed: Citizenship/immigration documents for all household members
Proof of all income for the past 30 days for all household members
Current electric and gas bills (front and back)
records.notes: Email info@eoac.org.
records.name: EOAC Energy Assistance (CEAP)
records.description_en: Help paying electric and gas bills, plus weatherization to make homes more energy efficient.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Households at or below 150% of federal poverty guidelines in McLennan and nearby counties.
records.how_to_apply: Download the application from EOAC's website and mail, fax, or drop it off with your documents at 1800 N. Valley Mills, Waco.

records.notes: Eligibility and documents not listed online; funding may be limited.
records.name: EOAC Emergency Assistance
records.description_en: Crisis help with essentials such as food, water, temporary housing, and rent and utility assistance.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Families in crisis in EOAC's service area; call for current rules.
records.how_to_apply: Call EOAC at (254) 753-0331.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Brazos, Burleson, Grimes, Leon, Madison, Montgomery, Robertson, Walker, Waller, or Washington County

documents_needed: Photo ID for all household members over 18
Proof of income for all household members over 18 (or Income Declaration form)
records.notes: Documents must be resubmitted each year. Email bvcapcontact@bvcog.org.
records.name: BVCAP Utility Assistance
records.description_en: Help paying utility bills for eligible low-income households, with priority for vulnerable households.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Households in Brazos and nearby counties who meet state and federal program income rules.
records.how_to_apply: Applications are by appointment only. Apply through the online portal or get help in person or by phone at the Bryan office.

records.notes: Sites include Brazos Head Start (3005 Edna Ave.), Johnette Hicks (510 S. 12th St.), New Road (1407 N. New Road), Woodrow Logan (3510 Latimer Dr.), all in Waco.
records.name: EOAC Head Start / Early Head Start
records.description_en: Free early learning, meals, and health screenings for babies, toddlers, and preschoolers.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Families in McLennan and Falls counties who meet federal income guidelines, receive TANF, SNAP, or SSI, are homeless, or have a child in foster care. Early Head Start serves children up to 3; Head Start serves ages 3-5.
records.how_to_apply: Call the enrollment line at (254) 304-7575, apply online in English or Spanish, or apply in person at any EOAC site.

documents_needed: At least two verifications of income for the past 12 months
records.notes: Centers: Bryan CDC, 711 Houston, Bryan (979) 775-5492; Neal CDC, 1306 Barak Lane, Bryan (979) 260-2679; Early Head Start, 3400 S. Texas Ave. Suite 7, Bryan (979) 846-5782.
records.name: BVCAP Head Start / Early Head Start
records.description_en: Early childhood education and care for young children from low-income families in Bryan.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Children ages 6 weeks to 4 years from families under the federal poverty income guidelines.
records.how_to_apply: Complete an application with the Head Start office and bring income proof, birth certificate, and shot records.

documents_needed: School enrollment verification if in training
records.cost: Parent share of cost based on income
records.notes: TX3C support 1-888-265-6461. Application status questions: ccswaitlist@hotworkforce.com. Hour and age rules from https://www.childcare.texas.gov/for-families/child-care-scholarships. There may be a waitlist.
records.name: Child Care Services - Workforce Solutions for the Heart of Texas
records.organization: Workforce Solutions for the Heart of Texas
records.description_en: State-funded child care scholarships that help pay for child care so parents can work or go to school or training.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Families in McLennan and nearby counties who need care to work or attend school or training (average 25 hours/week for single parents, 50 combined for two parents), for children birth to 12 (up to 18 with disabilities), and who meet income limits.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online through the TWC Texas Child Care Connection (TX3C) Parent Central portal.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Brazos, Burleson, Grimes, Leon, Madison, Robertson, or Washington County

records.cost: Parent share of cost based on income, household size, and number of children
records.notes: Phone extension 2105. Email CCMS@bvcog.org. Income limit is 85% of state median income (not FPL).
records.name: Child Care Assistance - Workforce Solutions Brazos Valley
records.description_en: Help paying for child care so parents can work, look for work, or attend school or training.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Families in Brazos and nearby counties with income at or below 85% of state median income. Single parents need 25 hours/week (two parents 50 combined) of work, job search, training, or school. Children under 13, or under 19 if disabled.
records.how_to_apply: Log in or create an account in TX3C to apply online.

records.notes: Hours not listed on the center locations page. Email questions@hotworkforce.com.
records.name: Workforce Solutions for the Heart of Texas - McLennan County Center
records.organization: Workforce Solutions for the Heart of Texas
records.description_en: Free job search help, hiring events, career workshops, training funds, veteran services, and unemployment help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Job seekers in McLennan, Bosque, Falls, Freestone, Hill, and Limestone counties.
records.how_to_apply: Visit the McLennan County center or call (866) 982-9226.

documents_needed: Proof of eligibility to work in the U.S.
Proof of income or unemployment/TANF/SNAP eligibility
records.notes: Income thresholds on page range from $13,590 (1 person) to $59,927 (10 people). Only one of the three criteria (low income, layoff, TANF/SNAP) is needed. Toll-free 1-866-982-9226.
records.name: WIOA Training Funds - Workforce Solutions for the Heart of Texas
records.organization: Workforce Solutions for the Heart of Texas
records.description_en: Pays for job training such as tuition, books, tools, uniforms, and certification exams, plus job search help and child care while in training.
records.eligibility_summary_en: People who can work in the U.S. and are low-income, were laid off through no fault of their own and are eligible for unemployment, or get TANF or SNAP.
records.how_to_apply: Submit the online WIOA application; a career specialist will contact you. Or call (254) 296-5341.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: McLennan, Bosque, Falls, Freestone, Hill, or Limestone County

records.name: EOAC EmpowerU Job Training
records.description_en: Job training and certifications such as CDL truck driving, HVAC, CNA, pharmacy tech, welding, and medical billing, with help paying for tuition, books, and supplies.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Residents of McLennan, Bosque, Falls, Freestone, Hill, or Limestone County who meet federal income guidelines.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online through EOAC's website or call (254) 753-0331.

records.name: Workforce Solutions Brazos Valley - Brazos County Center
records.description_en: Free job search help, resource room, job training (WIOA), adult education, veteran services, and SNAP and Choices employment programs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Job seekers in the Brazos Valley. WIOA adult training is for people 18+ who meet low-income rules; veterans and public assistance recipients get priority.
records.how_to_apply: Visit the Bryan center or call (979) 595-2800.

records.hours: Killeen: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri 8:30 AM-5 PM; Wed 8:30 AM-4 PM
records.notes: Temple center: 201 Santa Fe Way, Temple, TX 76502, (254) 742-4400, Mon-Wed & Fri 8:30-5, Thu 8:30-4. Website is partly under construction; the board likely also serves Coryell County but this was not confirmed on the page. Child care applications go through TX3C: https://childcare.twc.texas.gov/find/welcome.
records.name: Workforce Solutions of Central Texas - Killeen & Temple Centers
records.description_en: Workforce centers offering job search help, training, veteran services, vocational rehabilitation, and child care assistance.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Job seekers and families in Bell County and the Central Texas workforce area.
records.how_to_apply: Visit or call the Killeen center at (254) 200-2000 or the Temple center at (254) 742-4400.

records.notes: Local office street address and phone were not shown on the offices page; use the toll-free intake line. Some special projects allow higher income. Income info from https://www.lonestarlegal.org/get-help/.
records.name: Lone Star Legal Aid - Waco Office
records.description_en: Free civil legal help for low-income people, such as housing and eviction, family, and benefits problems. No criminal cases.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Low-income residents of Bosque, Falls, Freestone, Hill, Limestone, McLennan, and Navarro counties who meet income and legal status rules (generally up to 125% of the federal poverty level).
records.how_to_apply: Apply online through Lone Star Legal Aid's website or call toll-free (800) 733-8394. Calls are confidential.

records.notes: Local office street address and phone were not shown on the offices page; use the toll-free intake line. Some special projects allow higher income. Income info from https://www.lonestarlegal.org/get-help/.
records.name: Lone Star Legal Aid - Belton Office
records.description_en: Free civil legal help for low-income people, such as housing and eviction, family, and benefits problems. No criminal cases.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Low-income residents of Bell, Coryell, Hamilton, Lampasas, and Milam counties who meet income and legal status rules (generally up to 125% of the federal poverty level).
records.how_to_apply: Apply online through Lone Star Legal Aid's website or call toll-free (800) 733-8394. Calls are confidential.

records.notes: Local office street address and phone were not shown on the offices page; use the toll-free intake line. Some special projects allow higher income. Income info from https://www.lonestarlegal.org/get-help/.
records.name: Lone Star Legal Aid - Bryan Office
records.description_en: Free civil legal help for low-income people, such as housing and eviction, family, and benefits problems. No criminal cases.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Low-income residents of Brazos, Burleson, Grimes, Lee, Leon, Madison, and Robertson counties who meet income and legal status rules (generally up to 125% of the federal poverty level).
records.how_to_apply: Apply online through Lone Star Legal Aid's website or call toll-free (800) 733-8394. Calls are confidential.

records.hours: Mon-Fri 5 a.m.-7 p.m.; Sat 6 a.m.-8 p.m.
records.cost: $1.50 full fare; $0.50 reduced; paratransit $3 per trip
records.name: Waco Transit System (Reduced Fares & Paratransit)
records.organization: City of Waco - Waco Transit System
records.description_en: City buses, on-demand rides, county routes, and paratransit in Waco, with reduced fares for seniors, Medicare holders, and riders with disabilities.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Seniors and Medicare cardholders ride for $0.50 with a Waco Transit ID; riders with disabilities pay $0.50 after approval. Children 5 and under ride free; students at Baylor, MCC, TSTC, and Waco ISD ride free with school ID.
records.how_to_apply: Call (254) 750-1900 to get a Waco Transit reduced-fare ID or apply for disabled fare or paratransit.

records.notes: Specific reduced-fare eligibility not detailed on home page.
records.name: The HOP - Hill Country Transit District
records.description_en: Public buses, microtransit, commuter routes, rural demand-response rides, and ADA paratransit in Bell, Coryell, and Milam counties.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to the public in Killeen, Temple, Belton, Copperas Cove, Harker Heights, and rural areas. Reduced fares are available; call for rules.
records.how_to_apply: Book rides with the HOP app or online booking tool, or call (254) 933-3700.

records.notes: Existing clients can book at https://portal.btd.org.
records.name: Brazos Transit District
records.description_en: Public buses, ADA paratransit, and demand-response rides in Bryan, College Station, and rural areas, with reduced-fare senior and disabled passes.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to the public. Seniors and people with disabilities can apply for a reduced-fare pass.
records.how_to_apply: New demand-response riders call the Dispatch Center at (979) 778-4480 or (800) 272-0039. Apply for a Senior & Disabled Pass using the application on the website.

records.notes: Cost of services not stated on site.
records.name: Brazos Valley Affordable Housing Corporation - Homebuyer Counseling & Financial Fitness Center
records.description_en: Homebuyer counseling, affordable homes for sale, and one-on-one financial coaching.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Low- and moderate-income residents of Brazos County (and Caldwell area).
records.how_to_apply: Call (979) 595-2809 to schedule counseling or coaching.
